expert_blurbs.author: headChopper
expert_blurbs.text: Most of us are very anxious to see what Mike McDaniel can do with Justin Herbert. This seems like an extremely winnable matchup for Herbert, and the price tag is actually cheaper than I would have expected.

expert_blurbs.author: Notorious
expert_blurbs.text: I can’t wait to see what this Chargers’ offense looks like with Mike McDaniel at the helm. He’s one of the best offensive minds in football, and now that he’s an offensive coordinator instead of a head coach, he can focus on what he does best. Justin Herbert ($6,100 DK / $7,600 FD) has immense talent, but something always seems to go wrong with the Chargers. More often than not, it’s injuries to the offensive line or his wideouts. Neither is an issue heading into this season. McDaniel will make Herbert’s job a lot easier this season. The pre-snap motion and play-action will give Herbert easy throws and create space for the receivers. I want to bet on this offense early, especially in a home matchup against the Cardinals, who had a bottom-10 pass defense last season.

expert_blurbs.author: BobbyGomes
expert_blurbs.text: Everyone should be excited to see Justin Herbert under Mike McDaniels offense and he is simply too cheap on both sites. Highest implied offense on the slate, and isn't afraid to use his legs. Hard to ignore his value and upside on this slate and the Cards make for a compelling runback.

players.notes: Pre-snap motion and play-action give him easy throws against Arizona.

expert_blurbs.author: headChopper
expert_blurbs.text: This is easily the best group of weapons and the best offensive staff and system Kyler Murray has been a part of in the pros. Green Bay is likely to be tough on defense, but they will have to play the first portion of the season without their best player, Micah Parsons. I still believe there is a lot of untapped upside with Kyler Murray as a QB.

players.notes: Favorable system and weapons with Micah Parsons missing for Green Bay.
High team total in an indoor matchup against New Orleans.
Strong rushing floor with a solid implied team total of 44.5 points.

expert_blurbs.author: Notorious
expert_blurbs.text: Tyler Shough ($5,600 DK / $6,900 FD) led me to some nice DFS scores in the second half of last season. He played so well that the Saints decided that he didn’t need any reps in the preseason. While I would have given my young quarterback some reps, I’m not an NFL coach. Even though he’s missing one of his best weapons in Jordyn Tyson, I still love the spot for Shough in Week 1. He’s playing indoors against the Lions, who have a banged-up secondary heading into the season. He has two obvious stacking mates in Chris Olave and Juwan Johnson, and he offers rushing upside (35+ rushing yards in 3 of the last 5 games last season). It could also be a great game script for the passing attack, as the Saints are 6.5-point underdogs.

players.notes: Indoor matchup against a banged-up Lions secondary with strong rushing.
Solid home favorite spot with a team total in a favourable matchup.
Pass-heavy game script against Tampa Bay with a high 50.5 total.

expert_blurbs.author: DavisMattek
expert_blurbs.text: Caleb gets to start his season against a bottom half defense while Ben Johnson spent the offseason stating he wants to break the NFL record for points per game. Williams' year 1 to year 2 improvement is amongst the best in NFL history and we will be betting on more improvement in Year 3.

players.notes: Improved Year 2 progression facing a bottom-half Carolina defense.
Elite rushing floor as a home favourite against the Colts.
High ceiling as a home favourite in a competitive game environment.

expert_blurbs.author: vanekjordan
expert_blurbs.text: The Saints lost LB Demario Davis in free agency, and he was the leader of this defense for a long time. I don’t expect anyone on this roster to be able to replace him in Year 1, and that loss should hurt the run defense, which will lead to Gibbs feasting in this matchup.

expert_blurbs.author: Notorious
expert_blurbs.text: With David Montgomery now in Houston, we get a full season of Jahmyr Gibbs ($8,000 DK / $9,100 FD) as a bell-cow running back. There’s a reason why he’s been the de facto #1 pick in season-long drafts. He’s one of the most explosive players in the NFL, and he plays in one of the best offenses in the NFL. While the Saints are better equipped to stop the run than they are the pass, Gibbs can overcome a bad matchup, and he’s a huge weapon in the passing game. He’s a good bet for 20+ touches on an offense with a team total of 28.5 points. I’m not fading the best play on the board.

expert_blurbs.author: NeilCO
expert_blurbs.text: In a week where I generally think it's a good idea to embrace the unknown of a new season and get contrarian, I still think Gibbs is excellent chalk. He'll get all the work he can handle in a nice matchup. Gibbs should have a 5-figure DFS salary in no time.

expert_blurbs.author: BobbyGomes
expert_blurbs.text: Gibbs is the clear cut #1 RB on the slate, especially in Cash games. There is no more Montgomery (now with the Texans) and newly acquired backup Pacheco landed on IR to start off the season. That leaves Gibbs to freely occupy the running game with little red zone competition. Saints allowed the 11th most rushing YPG last season and have not made any major changes that would fix this.

players.notes: Bell-cow workhorse with massive touch projection against New Orleans.

expert_blurbs.author: headChopper
expert_blurbs.text: I think we are in for a nice bounce-back season from Saquon, and I do not believe the Commanders made enough acquisitions on defense to fill the holes they had last season. I believe they are likely to be average or below average again, and the Philly offensive line looks healthy heading into the season.

players.notes: Strong home favourite role with high touchdown equity.
Solid volume projection as a home favourite against Baltimore.

expert_blurbs.author: Notorious
expert_blurbs.text: I’m honestly a tad hesitant to tag Bijan Robinson ($7,700 DK) as a core play this week. On the one hand, he has little competition for touches now that Tyler Allgeier is out of the picture. The projected workload is essentially unmatched at the running back position. On the other hand, the Falcons are starting Cooper Rush at quarterback in a fairly difficult spot on the road against the Steelers. I suppose many will argue that Rush is a better quarterback at this stage than Tua Tagovailoa, but this offense as a whole carries systemic risk. I have Robinson tagged at the moment, but that could change by Sunday morning.

players.notes: Feature workload with little backfield competition in Pittsburgh.
High-volume workhorse role in a tight game script.
Explosive pass-catching back in a competitive road matchup.

expert_blurbs.author: ebeimfohr
expert_blurbs.text: With the absence of Brock Bowers, ownership is shifting heavily towards Michael Mayer and to a lesser degree Tre Tucker, but this is a smash spot for Jeanty. He is one of the most talented running backs in the league, and he should have a bounce back year two with Klint Kubiak in charge now. They revamped the offensive line, added Kirk Cousins (and Fernando Mendoza) and Jeanty is back fully healthy from a camp injury scare. I think this season with Kubiak is going to be a monster breakout for Jeanty, and the Dolphins are the worst team and worse defense in the league, but he is not projecting to be popular at all.

expert_blurbs.author: DavisMattek
expert_blurbs.text: Were Jeanty not injured at all in the preseason, this would likely be a spot that he would be the 4th most owned RB on the slate. I plan on deploying Jeanty in all SE/3-Max contests and will be bumping his projection in all of my sim runs against the worst team in the NFL.

players.notes: Bounce-back year behind a revamped offensive line against Miami.
Solid touches expected in a close divisional game environment.

expert_blurbs.author: vanekjordan
expert_blurbs.text: Lloyd is a starting RB under $5,000 on both sites who has a lot of talent and can get his work done as a pass catcher. The Vikings are going to lean on two rookie DTs, and that’s a very difficult position to excel at in Year 1. I think Lloyd has a great floor at a great price.

expert_blurbs.author: Notorious
expert_blurbs.text: MarShawn Lloyd ($4,900 FD) has one of the widest ranges of potential outcomes this week, but he’s too cheap on FanDuel to ignore. He’s cheap on DraftKings as well, but the FanDuel price sticks out like a sore thumb. The Packers drafted him with the 88th overall pick, and Josh Jacobs has been placed on the Commissioner’s Exempt List and is barred from practicing or playing entirely. Lloyd should be the lead back for Green Bay early in the season, but he was never a heavy-workload back in college. I’m hesitant to expect 20+ touches from him against the Vikings, but he’s still a great option at this price even if we only project him for 15 touches.

expert_blurbs.author: BobbyGomes
expert_blurbs.text: Lloyd is extremely underpriced given that he is the #1 with Jacobs sidelined. The Vikings are gambling on fixing their rushing woes with 2 rookies. Vikings allowed the 9th most rushing YPG last season, and its hard to imagine it gets better. Also to note, Lloyd is projected for sub 5% pOWN, when is the last time we have seen a sub 5k starting RB that low owned?

players.notes: Lead workhorse role with Josh Jacobs out against Minnesota.
Pass-catching role in a high-total game against Cincinnati.

expert_blurbs.author: DavisMattek
expert_blurbs.text: I am giving a slight preference to Chase over St. Brown this week due to ownership discrepancy and some secondary injuries for the Buccaneers' defense.

expert_blurbs.author: Notorious
expert_blurbs.text: There are some narratives that I buy into and others that I have a hard time believing. Joe Burrow and the Bengals have been notoriously slow starters, but every year brings a new team and new matchups, so I’m not shying away from them in Week 1. JaMarr Chase ($7,800 DK / $8,900 FD) is one of the best receivers in the NFL, and he has one of the best quarterbacks throwing him the ball. The Bengals open their season against the Buccaneers, who are expected to be one of the best pass-funnel matchups in the league. With Vita Vea leading the way, it will be extremely tough to run on Tampa Bay this season. We should see a pass-heavy game plan from the Bengals, which means there’s a good chance Chase will see double-digit targets. With the soft pricing, it’s easy to fit two expensive receivers in lineups.

expert_blurbs.author: BobbyGomes
expert_blurbs.text: Chase is a staple for cash and is hard to ignore facing a Bucs defense who should continue to blitz and play zone at a heavy rate. Ja'marr Chase has been one of the best WRs vs zone coverage over the last few seasons, averaging 3.28 yards per route run.

players.notes: Elite zone receiver facing a zone-heavy Tampa Bay defense.

expert_blurbs.author: Notorious
expert_blurbs.text: Chris Olave ($6,700 DK / $7,400 FD) was a prominent feature in my Key Personnel article last season. The advanced metrics continued to suggest positive regression, and sure enough, he finally started to have some breakout games. He was clearly the favorite target for Tyler Shough, as he racked up a 27% target share and a 42% air yards share with him under center. Olave is elite at creating separation and is a solid redzone threat. He draws a nice matchup against a banged-up Lions’ secondary in Week 1, and he doesn’t have much competition for targets with Jordyn Tyson out. You can pair him with Shough and bring it back with Jahmyr Gibbs, or you can use Olave as a bring-back to your Lions’ stacks.

players.notes: High target and air yards share against a banged-up Lions secondary.

expert_blurbs.author: DavisMattek
expert_blurbs.text: There is a chance that Garrett Wilson ends up leading the NFL in target share. He gets a matchup against a bottom-10 NFL defensive unit with a weak-ish pass rush outside of Jeff Simmons. Priced down on both DK and FD, Wilson a priority tournament option for me.

players.notes: Projected for massive target share against a weak Tennessee secondary.

expert_blurbs.author: BobbyGomes
expert_blurbs.text: Cardinals should continue to struggle to pressure and sack QBs which means Herbert will have plenty of time to torment this weak secondary. Chargers have the highest implied on the slate and their #1 Ladd McConkey is projected for sub 10% ownership.

players.notes: Primary slot option facing Arizona's vulnerable secondary.
Elite route participation in a competitive divisional matchup.
High target volume in an indoor game with a massive 49.5 total.
Deep threat role in a high-total game against Tampa Bay.
Solid target upside as a home favourite against Cleveland.

expert_blurbs.author: vanekjordan
expert_blurbs.text: DeVonta Smith has been incredible when A.J. Brown hasn’t been on the field, and now he’s the unquestioned alpha in this receiver room against a horrible Washington Commanders secondary. I know Jalen Hurts isn’t the greatest passer, but the hate has gone too far. They also made an upgrade at OC with Sean Mannion, and I expect Smith to be a major beneficiary.

players.notes: Unquestioned alpha role against a poor Washington secondary.
Deep threat perimeter role in a high-total game against Buffalo.

expert_blurbs.author: vanekjordan
expert_blurbs.text: McMillan is moving into the slot this year, and the Bears are without starting slot corner Kyler Gordon. This is a matchup McMillan should have a significant advantage over, and one the Panthers will look to attack.

players.notes: Moving to the slot against a Chicago defense missing Kyler Gordon.

expert_blurbs.author: vanekjordan
expert_blurbs.text: I thought Mayer would be the number 2 or 3 option with Brock Bowers in the lineup, and now he's probably the main target in the passing game. He's way too cheap.

expert_blurbs.author: Notorious
expert_blurbs.text: With Brock Bowers expected out, Michael Mayer ($2,900 DK / $4,600 FD) feels like the free square of the week (especially on DraftKings). The pricing is already soft as a whole, so plugging in Mayer essentially allows you to do whatever you want with the rest of your roster. I’m not sold on Kirk Cousins as being a good quarterback in his 15th NFL season, but he should be serviceable in a nice matchup against the Dolphins. In 4 games without Bowers last season, Mayer caught 18-of-24 targets for 196 yards and a touchdown.

expert_blurbs.author: NeilCO
expert_blurbs.text: Mayer is an obvious cash game play, but also a strong GPP target. He's cheap and could very easily lead the team in targets.

expert_blurbs.author: BobbyGomes
expert_blurbs.text: Very hard to ignore how cheap and expanded his role will be without Brock Bowers. He also gets the luxury of playing the Dolphins Week 1 who over the last few seasons have struggled to stop the TE position. Safe cash play with heavy ownership.

players.notes: Main target in the passing game with Brock Bowers sidelined.
Seam usage and red-zone role against Baltimore's linebackers.
Every-down route rate in a high-total divisional matchup.
Red-zone target volume in a high-total indoor matchup.
Strong route participation and seam usage against Minnesota.
Elite target volume and route rate against the Chargers.
Reliable seam option in a high-total indoor game.
Red-zone threat facing Washington's linebackers.

expert_blurbs.author: Notorious
expert_blurbs.text: Colston Loveland ($5,300 DK / $6,000 FD) could make the leap from a good tight end to a great tight end this season. It wouldn’t surprise me if he’s in the same tier as Trey McBride and Brock Bowers at the end of the season. The Bears want to break scoring records, and Loveland might be the most reliable weapon for Caleb Williams. Loveland really came alive at the end of last season, racking up 48 targets over the final 4 games (including the playoffs). Luther Burden and Rome Odunze are expected to suit up, but they’ve both dealt with injuries and haven’t had many reps with Williams leading up to Week 1.

players.notes: Reliable target volume in an explosive Chicago offense.
Red-zone role as a home favourite against Cleveland.
